summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary Box
summaryBox.takeaway: Organisms are organized into a mandatory nested hierarchy. Category = abstract rank (Class); Taxon = concrete biological entity (Mammalia). Moving down (Kingdom -> Species), shared traits and diagnostic precision INCREASE while organism count DECREASES.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TAXONOMIC HIERARCHY
                         
  RANK / CATEGORY                                TRENDS MOVING DOWN
     Kingdom             ▲                                │
     Phylum / Division   │ Decreasing Inclusivity        │ Increasing Specificity
     Class               │ Decreasing Number of Organisms │ Increasing Shared Traits
     Order               │ Increasing Similarity          │ Increasing Diagnostic Precision
     Family              │                                ▼
     Genus               │
     Species             │
conceptBreakdown.content:
Organisms are organized into a mandatory hierarchical system of nested categories. A Category represents an abstract rank or level in the hierarchy, whereas a Taxon (plural: Taxa) refers to a concrete biological entity assigned to that rank.

Example: "Class" is an abstract Category; "Mammalia" is a concrete Taxon.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Standardized Taxonomic Suffixes (Nomenclatural Endings)
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Standardized Taxonomic Suffixes (Nomenclatural Endings)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (ICNafp) mandates strict standardized suffix endings for taxonomic ranks. Animal nomenclature (ICZN) mandates endings primarily at the family level.

| Taxonomic Rank | Botanical Ending (ICNafp) | Fungal Ending | Algal Ending | Zoological Ending (ICZN) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Division / Phylum** | `-phyta` | `-mycota` | `-phyta` | Unstandardized |
| **Subdivision / Subphylum** | `-phytina` | `-mycotina` | `-phytina` | Unstandardized |
| **Class** | `-opsida` | `-mycetes` | `-phyceae` | Unstandardized |
| **Subclass** | `-idae` | `-mycetidae` | `-phycidae` | Unstandardized |
| **Order** | `-ales` | `-ales` | `-ales` | Unstandardized |
| **Suborder** | `-ineae` | `-ineae` | `-ineae` | Unstandardized |
| **Superfamily** | `-acea` | `-acea` | `-acea` | `-oidea` |
| **Family** | `-aceae` | `-aceae` | `-aceae` | `-idae` |
| **Subfamily** | `-oideae` | `-oideae` | `-oideae` | `-inae` |
| **Tribe** | `-eae` | `-eae` | `-eae` | `-ini` |
